summary: Strongest evidence for word-order rules in birds: ABC = scan for danger, D = approach, ABC-D is a compound with a distinct behavioural response; the reversed order D-ABC elicits nothing.

syllables.label: A note
syllables.function: component of the ABC alarm cluster (snake/predator vigilance)

syllables.label: B note
syllables.function: component of the ABC alarm cluster

syllables.label: C note
syllables.function: component of the ABC alarm cluster

songs.label: ABC
songs.function: receivers scan horizontally for a predator

songs.label: ABC-D
songs.gloss: scan for danger, then come here
songs.function: compound message; elicits both responses, more than the sum of its parts

songs.label: D-ABC (reversed)
songs.function: artificially reversed order; in playback experiments it elicits neither response

songs.label: learned bout
songs.gloss: a phrase in this bird's measured syntax

learnedFrom: Learned from 83 field recordings: 64 syllable types fitted from 4641 segmented syllables. No documented function is attached to any of them.
